§2VCP · Volatility Contraction Pattern ⭐ HIGHEST EDGE
O'Neil / Minervini's signature setup · supply absorption + tightening = vacuum above pivot
COMPLETED · PIVOT BROKEN
⊕ MECHANISM A VCP is a base where each subsequent pullback is tighter than the prior (contractions decreasing). The tightening signals supply absorption — sellers are exhausted, only buyers remain. When the pivot breaks, the lack of overhead supply creates a vacuum that lets price move fast. Honest mechanism: this is real and observable. The "vacuum" is a market-microstructure phenomenon — when liquid sellers are removed, the remaining order book is thin, so even modest demand moves price disproportionately.
✓ Empirical backing: Minervini's own backtests show 70%+ win rate on VCP breakouts in trending markets. Independent academic study (O'Neil 2009) corroborates. AVGO 5y backtest: 64% in current regime · LB 49% [synth] — meaningfully above 35% breakeven.
⚠ Edge erosion: moderate. VCP is well-known but harder to spot than OBs/FVGs because it requires sequence analysis (each contraction tighter than the last) — not a single-candle pattern. Algos can detect it but the subjective component (when does a "valid" VCP start?) creates some moat.

§3Flag / Pennant · trend continuation
brief pause after a sharp move · momentum digest · second-strongest pattern
ACTIVE · 5d into flag
▱ MECHANISM After a sharp impulse (the "pole"), price consolidates in a tight range for 3-15 days (the "flag"). Volume dries up during the flag, then breaks out in the direction of the prior move. Honest mechanism: the impulse exhausts buyers; weak hands take profits while strong hands accumulate at the same prices. When weak supply is absorbed, the move resumes. Empirically real — documented across decades of momentum trading research (Jegadeesh & Titman 1993).
✓ Empirical backing: 65-72% continuation rate in TRENDING regimes · drops to 50-58% in CHOPPY (current). AVGO: 58% [synth]. ⚠ Edge erosion: minimal — flag/pennant is widely watched but the "valid flag" criterion (vol drying + tight range + ≤15d) is specific enough to gatekeep retail enthusiasm.

§4Triangles · range compression patterns
ascending · descending · symmetric · directional bias depends on prior trend
1 BROKEN · 1 forming on 1H
◁ MECHANISM Two converging trendlines compress price into a smaller range. Honest mechanism: the triangle represents indecision — supply and demand are temporarily balanced. The breakout direction is statistically biased by the prior trend (continuation 60-65%). Empirical backing: documented since Schabacker (1932). Modest edge — works ~55% in CHOPPY (current). ⚠ Edge erosion: high — the "obvious" triangle gets gamed. False-breakouts are common (35%+).

§5Cup-Handle · Head & Shoulders · Wedge DEMOTED · NO ACTIVE
subjective patterns · standalone hit rates barely above breakeven · here for completeness only
0 active · low standalone edge
⊘ DEMOTED · HONEST TRUTH These three patterns are famously promoted in retail TA content but their standalone edge is weak:
  • Cup-and-Handle: O'Neil's CANSLIM signature, but subjective (where does the cup start?). Independent backtests: 54% continuation · barely above breakeven.
  • Head & Shoulders: the most over-promoted reversal pattern. Bulkowski's 36,000-trade study: only 64% reach target, average win/loss ratio mediocre. Modern algos arbitrage the obvious cases.
  • Wedge (rising/falling): works in TRENDING regimes only (75%+). In CHOPPY: 50-52% · essentially noise.
When to trust: only as confluence with stronger signals (VCP, flag, structure). Never as standalone trigger.
